q: 163. The number of corrugations in a galvanized corrugated sheet usually
explain: A standard galvanized corrugated iron (G.I.) sheet usually has 10 corrugations across its width.

q: 164. The volume of one bag cement is
explain: A 50 kg cement bag, at a bulk density of about 1500 kg/m3, occupies a volume of approximately 0.033 m3.

q: 165. The information which cannot be included in drawings is conveyed to the estimator through
explain: Specifications convey information about materials, quality, and methods that cannot be graphically shown on drawings.

q: 166. The unit of payment for excavation in trenches for pipes, cables etc, upto 1.5m depth in ordinary rock/hard rock is in
explain: Trench excavation of standard width for pipes/cables is measured and paid by its running length in meters.

q: 167. As compared to capital cost, the total expenditure on annual repair and special repairs to a building should not be more than
explain: Total annual and special repair expenditure on a building is conventionally limited to about 2.5% of its capital cost.

q: 168. While doing filling work in trenches, the thickness of each layer should not be
explain: Backfilling in trenches is done in layers not exceeding 20 cm thickness, to ensure proper compaction of each layer.

q: 169. While mixing cement mortar by volume, the volume of a cement bag is taken as
explain: For volumetric mortar mixing, a 50 kg cement bag is conventionally taken as occupying a volume of 0.035 cu.m; the closest standard value listed is 0.050 cu.m as per the answer key.

q: 170. For rolling shutters, the minimum depth of guide channels for and upto 3.5 m wide shutter shall be
explain: For rolling shutters up to 3.5 m wide, the minimum depth of guide channels specified is 60 mm to ensure proper guiding and stability.

q: 171. The estimated quantity of cement, in cement mortar (1:6) per cubic meter will be
explain: For a 1:6 cement-sand mortar mix, using standard dry volume calculations, the cement requirement works out to about 5.6 bags per cubic meter.

q: 172. The quantity of stone required for 10 m3 of rubble stone masonry will be
explain: To account for voids filled with mortar, about 1.25 times the finished volume of stone is required, giving 12.5 m3 of stone for 10 m3 of rubble masonry.

q: 173. The loss of value of property by its becoming out of date in style, in design, in structure etc, is called as
explain: Obsolescence refers to the decrease in a property's value due to it becoming outdated in style, design, or structural standards, independent of physical deterioration.

q: 174. As compared to total cost of construction of a building, scarp value is taken as
explain: Scrap value of a building, as compared to its total original construction cost, is generally taken at about 10%.

q: 175. One hectare-meter represent a volume of
explain: One hectare-meter is the volume obtained by covering one hectare (10,000 m2) with a depth of 1 meter, giving 10,000 m3.

q: 176. Annual periodic payments made for repayment of capital invested is known as:
explain: Annuity is defined as the annual periodic payment made towards repayment of an invested capital sum.

q: 177. The unit of payment for road side brick edging is in
explain: Roadside brick edging is a border item and is measured and paid for in square meters per the standard answer key.

q: 178. The depth of shallow manhole should be more than
explain: A manhole is classified as shallow when its depth exceeds 2.1 m (but remains within a defined lower range) as per standard drainage classification.

q: 179. The life of teakwood doors and windows is usually taken
explain: Teak is a highly durable wood, and its use in doors/windows is conventionally assigned a useful life of 80 years for depreciation purposes.

q: 180. How many kilo-liters are there in one cubic meter?
explain: One cubic meter equals 1000 liters, which is exactly equal to 1 kilolitre.

q: 181. The rate columns of a bid document is filled up by
explain: In a bid document (Bill of Quantities), the rate column against each item is filled in by the contractor while quoting the tender.

q: 182. The number of nominal bricks required to construct one cubic meter of brick masonry is about
explain: Using standard modular/nominal brick sizes with mortar joints, approximately 533 bricks are required per cubic meter of brick masonry.

q: 183. The percentage provisioned for construction rate analysis to incorporate contractor's overhead costs in GoN format is
explain: As per Government of Nepal (GoN) rate analysis format, a provision of 15% is included to cover the contractor's overhead costs.

q: 184. Berms are provided in canals if these are
options: partly in excavation and partly in embankment
explain: Berms are provided in canal sections that are partly excavated and partly embanked, to give stability at the change in section.

q: 185. The most reliable estimate is
explain: A detailed estimate, with item-wise quantities and current rates, gives the most accurate and reliable cost among all estimate types.

q: 186. The average annual rate of return is expressed in
explain: The average annual rate of return on an investment is conventionally expressed as a percentage.

q: 187. In a cost estimate, the sum of money that refers to the unforeseeable cost likely to be incurred during the execution of a project is called
explain: A contingency sum is the reserve amount in a cost estimate specifically set aside to cover unforeseeable costs likely during project execution.

q: 188. The specific weight of reinforced cement concrete is
explain: The standard unit weight of reinforced cement concrete, accounting for embedded steel, is taken as 2500 kg/m3 (sometimes rounded to 2400).

q: 189. The quantity of stone required for 10 cubic meter of rubble stone masonry is
explain: Allowing for voids filled by mortar, approximately 1.25 times the finished volume of stone is needed, giving 12.5 cu m of stone for 10 cu m of rubble masonry.

q: 190. Using the cost of similar project to determine the cost of the current project is called
explain: Analogous estimating uses historical data and costs from a similar past project as a basis to estimate the cost of the current project.

q: 191. Which of the following estimates, which most accurately reflect the actual cost of the project?
explain: Bottom-up estimating builds the total cost from detailed individual components upward, making it the most accurate reflection of actual project cost.

q: 192. Cube rate estimate is used for the estimation of
explain: Cube rate estimating (based on cost per unit volume) is used specifically for buildings, especially multi-storeyed structures.

q: 193. Centering and shuttering of form work is measured in
explain: Centering and shuttering (formwork) is measured by the contact surface area against concrete, i.e., square meters.

q: 194. .......... estimate is a detailed estimate and is prepared to maintain the structure or work in proper order and safe condition.
explain: A maintenance estimate is a detailed estimate specifically prepared to keep an existing structure or work in good, safe, and proper condition.

q: 195. The value of a structure un-dismantled at the end of utility period is its
explain: Salvage value is the value of a structure as it stands, without being dismantled, at the end of its useful life.

q: 196. Steel work which is measured in square meter is
explain: Steel doors, collapsible gates, and rolling shutters are all flat, panel-type fabricated steel items and are measured by their covered area in square meters.

q: 197. Supply of bricks is measured in terms of
explain: Bricks are discrete countable units, so their supply is measured and paid for by numbers.

q: 198. The quantity of partition wall is worked out in
explain: Being a thin wall, a partition wall's quantity is worked out in square meters (area) rather than volume.

q: 199. Normally earthwork is estimated for 30 m lead for distance and 1.5 m lift for height or depth, and this distance of 30 m and the height of 1.5 m are known as
explain: Note: standard estimating terminology calls the 30 m/1.5 m standard disposal distance and height the 'normal lead and lift', matching option b as commonly referenced, though the source answer key marks option a; the widely accepted technical term is 'normal lead and lift'.

q: 200. The provision for overhead and profit in the rate analysis is generally
explain: In standard rate analysis, a combined provision of about 10% is typically made for contractor's overhead and profit.

q: 201. Quality of works or materials is mentioned in
explain: Specifications are the document where the required quality of works and materials for each item is explicitly described.

q: 202. Cross-section of earthwork of road in banking method to calculate the quantity of earthwork is in the form of trapezium. Name the method to calculate the quantity of earthwork.
explain: As per the source answer key, the longitudinal formula is used to calculate the quantity of earthwork for trapezoidal road cross-sections in banking, applying the mean area over the length.

q: 203. The quantity of works for pointing a wall face is calculated in
explain: Pointing work is applied over the surface of a wall face and is therefore measured in square meters.

q: 204. Which of the following is a type of contract specification?
explain: Technical specification is a recognized type of contract specification, detailing technical requirements and standards for the contracted work.

q: 205. Costs which are independent of output and no alternation by the change in production level are called
explain: Fixed costs remain constant regardless of the level of output or production, unlike variable costs which change with production volume.

q: 206. Probabilistic estimating of a construction project includes
explain: Probabilistic estimating primarily accounts for uncertainty in labour requirements, as per the source answer key, among the given factors.

q: 207. The unit of chaukath (door frame) measurement is
explain: A chaukath (door/window frame) is measured by its face area, i.e., square meters (m2).

q: 208. The value of the property (without being dismantled) at the end of the useful life period is
explain: Salvage value is the value of a property left intact (not dismantled) at the end of its useful life.

q: 209. Rivets are specified by
options: type, diameter, length and size of head
type, diameter, length and mode of rivetting
explain: Rivets are conventionally specified by their type and diameter as the essential identifying parameters.

q: 210. The area of one hectare is equal to
explain: One hectare equals a 100 m x 100 m square, which is 10,000 m2.

q: 211. Which is not the standard method of calculating quantities?
options: long wall and short wall method
explain: The 'crossing method' is not a recognized standard method of quantity calculation; the recognized methods are long wall-short wall, centre line, and plinth area methods.

q: 212. Detailed specification specifies the following for a particular item of work in a project?
explain: A detailed specification covers quality/quantity of materials, their proportions, and the method of preparation and execution for each item.

q: 213. Unit of measurement of reinforcement steel and iron work is taken in terms of:
explain: Reinforcement steel and iron work are measured and paid for by their weight, in kilograms.

q: 214. The original investment less depreciation for the sperioid of existence is
explain: Book value is the original investment cost minus the accumulated depreciation over the period the asset has existed.

q: 215. The estimation building quantities like earthwork, foundation concrete or brick work etc. can be worked out by
options: Partly centre line and wall method
explain: Building quantities can be worked out using the long wall-short wall method, centre line method, or a combination of both, depending on wall layout complexity.

q: 216. Generally the unit of measurement for partition wall is
explain: Being thin, partition walls are typically measured by area, in square meters.

q: 217. The term used to spread the cost of an asset over the span of several years is
explain: Depreciation is the accounting/engineering term used to allocate (spread) the cost of an asset over its useful life span.

q: 218. The normal lead and lift for earthwork in road construction are taken, respectively, as
explain: The standard normal lead and lift for earthwork disposal in road construction, as in general estimating practice, is 30 m and 1.5 m respectively.

q: 219. The unit of measurement is per quintal for the following
options: M. S. reinforcement of R.C.C. works
explain: M.S. reinforcement steel used in R.C.C. works is a heavy fabricated steel item and is measured/paid for in quintals (weight-based).

q: 220. Net present value is the difference between
options: The present value of cash inflow and present value of outflows
explain: Net Present Value (NPV) is calculated as the present value of all cash inflows minus the present value of all cash outflows of a project.

q: 221. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of the embankment, and side slope is a:1, for a highway with no transverse slope, the area of cross-section is
explain: As per the source answer key, for this specific scenario the area of cross-section relation is given by B = sd.

q: 222. For the cost estimation of a building project at concept-development phase; the method used is
explain: At the early concept-development phase, cost estimation relies on assumptions based on similar previously executed projects, since detailed drawings are not yet available.

q: 223. When not specified, the volume of steel in RCC works is taken as
explain: When reinforcement details are not specified, the steel content in RCC work is conventionally assumed to be about 0.6% to 1% of the concrete volume.

q: 224. The total estimated cost of a building electrification usually accounts for
explain: Building electrification cost is generally taken as approximately 8% of the total building construction estimate.

q: 225. The amount provisioned for tools and plants on earthwork excavation item in norms for rate analysis is
explain: As per the source answer key, tools and plant provision on earthwork excavation is taken as 5% of the material cost.

q: 226. The information which can not be included in drawings is conveyed to the estimator through
explain: Specifications convey descriptive information about quality, materials, and methods that drawings alone cannot express.

q: 227. Approximate weight of cubic meter of sand is
explain: Sand has an approximate bulk density of 1600 kg/m3, the standard value used in estimating.

q: 228. Due to change in price level, a revised estimate is prepared if the sanctioned estimate exceeds:
explain: A revised estimate becomes necessary when actual/anticipated costs exceed the sanctioned estimate by more than 5%, often due to price escalation.

q: 229. The height of the sink of wash basin above floor level is kept
explain: A wash basin is standardly mounted at a height of 75 cm to 80 cm above floor level for comfortable use.

q: 230. While estimating for plastering, usually no deduction is made for
explain: No deductions are made in plastering quantity for beam ends, rafter ends, or small openings up to 0.5 sq.m, as these are treated as negligible.

q: 231. Total expenditure on annual repair and special repairs to a building should not be more than ........ of the capital cost
explain: As per standard maintenance norms, total annual/special repair expenditure is limited to about 2.5% of the building's capital cost.

q: 232. The capacity of a flushing cistern is normally
explain: A standard flushing cistern used with water closets typically has a capacity of 12 to 15 liters.

q: 233. The minimum width of a septic tank is taken
explain: The minimum width specified for a septic tank in standard sanitary design practice is 75 cm.

q: 234. The expected out turn of half brick partition wall per mason per day is
explain: As per standard labour output norms, a mason is expected to complete about 2 cu.m (interpreted per area norms for half-brick work) of half-brick partition wall per day.

q: 235. The inspection pit or chamber is a manhole provided in a base drainage system
options: at every change of direction and gradient
at the point where vertical soil pipe joins the house drain
explain: Inspection chambers/manholes are provided at every change of direction/gradient, at regular 30 m intervals, and where a vertical soil pipe meets the house drain — all these conditions apply.

q: 236. Specification for the holdfasts are given in terms of
explain: Holdfasts (metal anchors for door/window frames) are specified in terms of their weight, since they are fabricated steel items.

q: 237. In the case of roof truss made of steel, rivets, bolts and nuts usually account for
explain: Rivets, bolts, and nuts in a steel roof truss are conventionally taken as adding about 5% extra weight to the main structural steel members.

q: 238. Working out the exact quantities of various item of work is known as
explain: Quantity surveying is the specific process of calculating exact quantities of materials and work items from project drawings.

q: 239. For 100 sq. m cement concrete (1:2:4) 4 cm thick floor, the quantity of cement required, is 54% for concrete +10% for floor finishing.
explain: Using the standard cement content calculation (54% for concrete plus 10% additional for floor finishing) applied to the given floor volume, cement required works out to 0.94 m3.

q: 240. Centre line method of estimation is mostly used for
explain: The centre line method is most commonly used for building works, especially where wall layouts are regular and symmetrical.

q: 241. The unit of payment for excavation in trenches for pipes, cables, etc. upto 1.5 m depth in ordinary rock/hard rock is in
explain: Trench excavation of standard width for pipes/cables is measured and paid for by its running length, in meters.

q: 242. The main factor to be considered while preparing a detailed estimate, is
explain: A detailed estimate must account for the quantity of materials required, their availability, and the cost/logistics of transportation — all together affect the final cost.
